reviews.comment: Unfortunately, Dr. Yancey has now retired from teaching at A&M as far as I am aware. However, while he was here, I enjoyed his lectures a lot. Granted, there was a point where I stopped showing up because I kept falling asleep without fail. Dr. Yancey is a great professor who cares about what he is teaching and makes it very easy to succeed.

The entire grade is made up of 3 online tests with all the information coming off the lecture slides that he posts. Prof obviously cares a lot about Geology and really wants to spread his knowledge and gives plenty of resources if you actually want to learn more about the topics he discusses. If you don't, it's still an easy A.

Professor Yancey was amazing! His lectures were very insightful and provided a lot of information. All the lecture slides were posted on Canvas, and the tests were open note. The test questions were taken directly from the lecture. There is an optional textbook for this course (I suggest getting it!).
reviews.ratingTags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Take Geology 101 if you want an easy A. No homework, no quizzes, and no mandatory attendance. There were three tests in total, all of which were online an open note and he posts all his slides on canvas so you don't even need to take notes. Overall I highly recommend taking Yancey's class.
Overall good professor, very passionate in lectures.

Yancey really is passionate about the subject and makes the class interesting. The only grades are the tests, so do well on those but they're super easy. Study his PowerPoints and you're good to go. Definitely would recommend to anyone who needs an easy A science credit.

Yancey is an amazing prof for GEOL 106! His lectures were interesting and made you think critically. I've never had a more passionate professor than him. Tests come straight from the lecture slides and are super straightforward. Be sure to actually try on the labs as they count for a large portion of your final grade.
Dr. Yancey is fun to listen to and he makes geology pretty interesting. This class was not very difficult and I'd recommend it to anyone who needs a science credit.
reviews.ratingTags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This was the easiest class I have taken in college. Three multiple choice exams that can each be completed in 10 minutes. Yancey is a good professor, but he is very quit and a bit dull. I slept through most lectures. However, Yancey is very passionate and you will learn a lot of practical information on geology

He's super passionate about geology but very boring. I stopped going to class about a month in and I still made an A. The exams are extremely easy and there's no homework, just the 3 exams. Great choice for an easy A

His lectures are boring but attendance is NOT mandatory which is nice. I went to class about 3 times the whole semester and still ended up with an A but I had to teach myself the material which wasn't hard at all. No hw or quizzes, just 3 exams the whole semester that of which are not cumulative! Definitely an easy A! TAKE HIM!

There were only 3 exams and those were the only scores that mattered. If you're a good test-taker, I highly recommend this class. Although the lectures were quite boring, it was an easy A. Most people didn't show up to class and still managed to get an A.

Lectures might be boring but he is very passionate about geology. Not a hard class at all, study the slides online and pass the 3 exams. No hw, no textbook. Attendance is non-mandatory. Above all, he is super nice but if you really want to learn, sit at the front in class because he has a soft voice. Would recommend for an easy A.

Professor Yancey provided very boring and straight forward lectures from a PPT. It is very hard not to fall asleep. His office hours arent worth much as he cant be any assistance and will just tell you to keep trying hard. Why did I even waste my time to go? Do yourself a favor and dont take him as a prof, I know others who did well with others

Dr. Yancey is a great professor. He does not make the topics too challenging and studying the powerpoints he posts online are the best way to prepare for his exams. Put effort into the labs, they are worth 25% of the final grade. He generally curves each exam depending on the average. He is 100% someone I recommend taking.

Very rude and disrespectful. He's been the only one teaching GEOL106 for the past 20 years, so good luck. Just study powerpoints, and pay attention to the smallest details. Don't ever attend his office hours unless you want to be called stupid.

Ignore every other review besides this one. Everyone on here is stupid. This class has no homework. All he does is lecture. Your only grades are 4 tests. All you have to do is study the powerpoints he posts online because he reads them word for word in class. If you want a blowoff class take this one. No textbook needed at all.
reviews.ratingTags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Yanceyis awesome if you're willing to put in the time to talk to him and get to know him. His lectures can be boring for people who don't love about geology, but it's still a good class. He turns into a little kid when covering dinosaurs, and he will definitely remember you if you ask questions or sharing cool stuff you find on the internet.
Went to about 50% of the classes and still got an A. The tests are the powerpoints and thats it.
reviews.ratingTags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Yancey obviously really loves geology and knows a lot. However, the lectures can be very very dry. Every question on the tests comes from the powerpoints he posts online so attendance isn't necessary. I showed up like 4 times and still got an A from just studying the powerpoints at home. Pretty easy A, but not very interesting.

The class is very lecture-heavy with 3 mid-terms and a final. There is homework, but it's only 5% of the final grade. Dr. Yancey is clearly knowledgeable about Geology (I didn't think someone could love rocks as much as he does), but I got the impression that he didn't care if his students fell behind.  Buy the book. That's where he gets his tests.

You will have four exams, and that's it. Almost all his test were covered in his slides(which he posts online) and he had "review questions" that if you knew about, you would make a solid grade. I stopped going to class after the first exam, and only studied for about an hour for each test(only studying the review questions) and made a solid B.

Professor Yancey was a nice enough guy, but your class grade is determined by the three non-cumulative midterms, and the cumulative final, with some online homework. He expects you to know the answer to questions before you ask them,  he expects you to apply the information from power points to use on test, so tests are not verbatim of lectures.

Not a hard class to get an A in if you study well. You do not need to go to class, he posts all the lectures on Ecampus and you don't need the textbook. Basically just study the power points for the test, he kinda mumbles during the lectures and goes on tangents during class. He doesn't really seem to care about the class.

I made an appointment with him to review my test, and he repeatedly said the answers I did not know were "obvious".  His class wasn't time consuming because there was no work, but I had to try to teach myself the material. He was knowledgable but did not present/explain it well. He does give you power points and sample test questions.

Yancey was a good prof, but is hard to hear during lectures. All of his notes are available to you online, but if you don't want to read the book, go to class. The online homeworks were the hardest part of this class because they were hard and time consuming. Overall good prof, study details for tests.

Yancey is very knowledgeable, but is not a teacher. You need to be able to learn on your own, because he just does not do a great job presenting the material. I only survived because we actually learned in my lab, but not from this class. Exams are 50 multiple choice questions and have a few stupid trick questions. Only grades are from 4 exams.
reviews.ratingTags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I'm a non-sciences major and this class wasn't too bad at all. He posts all his powerpoints online, but you need to understand the content if you want to pass. He doesn't take attendance which is a plus, and I never touched the "required" textbook. I did just fine.
Really boring lectures.  Have to read the book to pass.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Yancey is a solid professor. He really knows his stuff . He's good at teaching it and is a very fair grader. All the information comes from the power-points, there were occasional pop-quizzes but I don't believe they were added to the grade (unless you were borderline)  The lectures do occasionally become slightly dull but otherwise he is fine.

If you are a non-major looking for an easy A, look somewhere else. Yancey is a good prof but he expects you to actually listen to his lectures and care about the subject. He posts all his lectures online, so attendance isn't mandatory, but he does occasionally give some helpful test hints for those who actually attend class.

Yancey is funny as heck but not in a way you expect. More like, you laugh with your friends about him after the fact. He is very peculiar. This class seriously is just a sit and listen class and then read the powerpoints, do flash cards and boom you make a B. Good morning coffee class for sleepy people. Yancey doesn't change clothes btw. That's hot

Boy I tell you what I barely squeaked by with an A in this class, This lil man ain't the sweetest but he knows his stuff, Tests are based off of power points and I didn't bother buying a textbook, Provides the previous years final which was pretty handy, After the first test I went to about a class every other week

He really seems like a nice guy but class was always hard to sit through. His lectures are long and sometimes boring. All of the material you need for the tests comes from the lecture powerpoints that he posts online. He does give out sample questions before that tests that do appear on the actual exam. It's an A if you put the effort in and study.

The information for his tests are in the lectures, if you attend class and review the practice question he gives out before each test you will get an easy A in the class. I enjoyed his class and had a really easy time with it after the first test.

He is a average professor. His lectures are boring dry powerpoint slideshows. You probably should read your book if you want to get an A on his tests. His tests are multiple choice, yet tricky. Average class
Never used the book once. Everything is based on the power points that he posts on eCampus. Test are long and are kinda tough because of the amount of detail in the power points.

Dr. Yancey really knows his stuff. He reads off his power points and rambles on about other information that wont be on the tests. You don't really have to go to class since all power points are posted online. Tests are hard due to the amount of information and detail covered. Not a super approachable guy.

All lectures are posted on eCampus, in power point format. He just lectures straight from the power points. He's teaching style is boring, making it difficult to stay awake and focused. Grade is based on exams (4 including final) and lab. Study the power points for the exams and you'll be okay. Don't get the textbook, I never used it.

He's very rude to people in class and often just laughs at people when they get the courage to answer one of his questions. He seems to only want to make you feel stupid if you ask questions in his office. He's also very boring when lecturing, so don't even bother going to class, just study the online slides and you'll be fine.

Don't buy or rent the book.   Good lecturer. Organized. Fair grader. You can expect what will be on the tests, and that is whatever is on his slides. When studying, just focus on the slides. Go to class, study the slides, and you'll do fine. Doesn't seem like a very approachable fellow, but I don't care about that.

He was rude during office hours. Acted like he he didn't even want to teach. Honestly, I think he just teaches for the research money. Wasn't a terribly hard class, but he didn't do anything to make it easier.

Dr. Yancey is fun to have because of how much he loves his job. Who knew someone could love rocks so much. He gives all of the power points online, and he even gives sample questions for the tests. He is overall a good professor, but his class is pretty hard to stay focused in. Go to class and should do fine.

Dr. Yancey knows his stuff. Go to class and you should pass. He is very very interested in what he does. All of his power points are online, and he even gave sample question to all of his tests. Class is hard, but he is okay.
Dr. Yancey was nice and all but his class was pretty hard. All of the power points were online, and he even gave some sample questions that could be on all of the tests.

He really knows his stuff and is obviously into what he is teaching but it's hard to keep engaged in his class. He can be pretty condescending during office hours though he seems to (possibly?) be trying to help. Ok enough in class but overall leaves some to be desired.

Dr . Yancey is fun to have in class because of his love for Geology. Make sure and attend class because of random attendance quizzes. Test come straight from the notes but he always says to read the book.

Last semester is when Yancey seemed easy.  This semester he has bumped up the loadwork and reading.  Don't go to his office hours.  He won't answer your questions directly, and he's extremely rude.  He will call you stupid and won't hesitate to throw you out without helping you.  He knows what he's talking about, but he's a terrible prof

In general I would say this class was somewhat difficult. Prof loves his job and he's always excited about what he's teaching but still boring during lecture. Gives random attendance quizzes to boost grade but attendance is not always necessary. Posts all notes online and also posts sample questions before tests which are helpful.

Go to class because he does random attendance quizzes that he'll use to boost your grade later on. He has practice questions before each test. He goes by the book. He loves what he teaches and is always excited. His tests are a little difficult though.

Obvi rocks aren't interesting, but he's not that bad of a prof. He knows what he's talking about and is really excited about teaching it! He's a cute old guy too :) He has some atendance quizzes that in the end puts towards curves and boosting grades.
